brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: 6 bases (3 wide x 2 tall: piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;half-n, piece:1,0,0;full and the level-1 row) with 3 top covers (cover:-1,0,1;full;top, cover:0,0,1;half-n;top, cover:1,0,1;full;top) forming a continuous flat deck 507 x 384 mm, 160 mm tall, dressed with book-row (prop:1) and book-stack (prop:2). It is a low, flat shelf rather than a tall multi-tier bookcase.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and mesh collisions only: it knows nothing about materials, strength or load ratings, and the parts are 3D-printed plastic in a material the user chooses and prints. No 50 kg rating can be certified from this build; capOpenFaces and lockJoints (jointBolt:1#-1,0#0) stiffen the joints but do not establish a load capacity. The books shown are staging props, not a load test.
drawer:0#0,0#cut on the cut face of the half-n base at level 0 and drawer:1#0,0#cut on the half-n base at level 1, both in the middle cell (0,0), their tops level with the shelf deck.

finish.summary: Built a low, wide 507 x 384 x 160 mm shelf unit: three full/half bases wide by two storeys tall, with a continuous covered deck on top dressed with a row and a stack of books, capped open faces and bolted joints, and two drawers fitted in the middle column. check_build passes with meshClash clear and no prop warnings. The 50 kg load rating cannot be met or certified: the configurator verifies fit only, not strength, and the parts are 3D-printed plastic, so that requirement is honestly reported unmet rather than claimed.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A 50 kg book shelf with two drawers — I'll build the shelf shape and two working drawers, but I can't certify a load rating in printed plastic, so that claim will be marked honestly.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
